### Strengths

- **Every guard that exists has the test that fires it.** Of the 88 guard mutants, 81 are killed:
  all 11 of the edit engine's (the fingerprint check, the rollback, the stage, its removal, the
  file's access, a created file over an existing one, a file named twice, the retry), all 8 of the
  session's confinement, 9 of the 10 query path rules (network, dot segments, relative, NUL,
  device, sibling prefix, length; case folding survives, M4), 6 of the 7 language-server mutants
  (its refusals and the withdrawal of fixed findings; the cache forget survives, M4), the 3
  closed-pipe and interrupt handlers, and 44 of the 49 server gates - the token,
  the Bearer scheme, the cookie, the launch code spent, expired, compared by prefix, weakened,
  `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`, the content type, both body limits, `frame-ancestors`, `nosniff`,
  `Referrer-Policy`, the inline hash, every page-path rule, the cap, the lingering close, the IPv6
  hold and both exclusivities.
- **The campaign scores well above the core's**: 83.9 % of 2,520 (84.3 % of those a test reaches);
  every stratum between 77.1 % (cli) and 88.5 % (plugins); negated tests 166 of 167 (the other
  hung), deleted raises
  143 of 144, swapped arguments 141 of 144, comparisons 160 of 166, returns 150 of 157, deleted
  findings 11 of 11.
- **The heavy files earn their time.** `test_gui_api` runs last in every ask, so when it is the first
  to fail no other in-scope file reaching the line failed: it is the only killer of 169 mutants (110
  of the 268 kills in the gui-api stratum). `test_gui_server`, next to last, is the first killer of
  180.
- **Where a rule is written twice, the suite compares the two**, and those comparisons catch what the
  line map cannot select: the route table against the security page (`tests/test_gui_docs.py`, 8
  module-level survivors killed in the follow-up), the toolbox's severities against the guide
  (`tests/test_documentation.py:3341`, 3), `KEY_ORDER` against `PROPAGATED_KEYS`
  (`tests/test_variable_keys.py:92`, 2), every query model published (`tests/test_gui_api.py`, 2).
- **Isolation and hygiene hold**: no false kill among 36 null mutants and 88 guard mutants on twelve
  parallel copies with arbitrary subsets of tests; 297 of 301 re-asked mutants gave the same outcome,
  the four others explained above; one `time.sleep` in the 38 files, inside a deadline loop
  (`tests/test_gui_server.py:2053`); no coverage pragma anywhere in `src/ddd`, so the 100 % branch
  gate is real; the suite writes nothing into its tree.
- **Pass 11b's eighteen findings are fixed but two**, among them both Importants (table below).

### Issues

#### Critical

None. No survivor is a defect of today's code; each is a wrong program the suite would let through.
The defects that are present - passes 10, 13 and 19 - have no test, which is I1.

#### Important

  passes 10, 13 and 19 found by hand fails a test of 10 to 30 lines built from the suite's own
  helpers, and no such test is in the suite.**

  Why it is structural: the guards the code has are tested one refusal at a time and every one fires
  (Strengths); what is never built is a second actor - a second writer, a save inside the window, a
  second project, a second image, a buffer that is not the disk, a stream that closes on a run with a
  verdict. Passes 9, 10, 13 and 19 named their own cases in their Test gaps; what this adds is that
  the ten tests are short, need no fixture the suite lacks, run in about a second, and fail today, so
  each fix can land with its test (S, about an hour each).

### Open questions

1. Is a second actor - a second writer, a save inside an analysis, a second project or image, an
   open buffer, a closed stream on a run with a verdict - something the suite must hold, as a rule?
   I1's probes show it can be done without threads or sleeps. The answer decides whether the fixes of
   passes 10, 13 and 19 land with their tests, and whether M1's test is a rule or a defect.
2. Is a stock Windows, without long paths, a supported development machine (M8)? If yes, two tests
   change; if no, the developer page says so.
3. Should a contributor be able to run "what matters" for a module in seconds - a `slow` marker on
   `test_cmake` and `test_gui_server`, `pytest-xdist`, a map from module to test files (the line map
   used here is one) - or is the whole suite before a commit the intended loop? The developer page's
   timing and advice follow the answer.

### Assessment

The periphery's suite is better than the core's by every measure this pass took: every guard the
code has fires a test when removed, 84 % of mutants die against the core's 72 %, the heavy files
are not redundant, and it is isolated enough to run on twelve copies at once without a false kill.
Its failure is of a different kind, and more serious than a score says: it tests what the code
already refuses, one refusal at a time, and never builds the second actor that every hand-found
defect of passes 10, 13 and 19 needs - a second writer, a save in the window, a second project or
image, a buffer unlike the disk, a closed stream on a failing run. Each of those ten defects fails a
short test written from the suite's own helpers, and none is there; one test even pins the shared
stage name behind pass 13's lost description. Around that, the gaps are the ordinary ones of a large
suite with one-entry fixtures and expectations read from the code under test: an undo that offers
the wrong edit, a doubled warning count, an empty token accepted by a weakened compare, all green.
The runtime is honest but undocumented: nine to eleven minutes in one process, two thirds of it in
two files, and no smaller loop offered. 100 % coverage here means every line ran; it does not mean
the hazards the reader of passes 10 and 13 met were ever tried.

**M1 (refuted).** `tests/test_editing.py:718-719` asserts `STAGING_SUFFIX == ARTEFACT_STAGING_SUFFIX`. That pins how the suffix is spelled, not whether two writes share a stage. Pass 22's own crude fix gives each write a stage name of its own and keeps the suffix (`fx22`, `editing.py:931`). On that copy the test passes, and so does its twin for `ddd id`, `tests/test_cli.py:3586-3589`, which M1 does not name (`logs/fx22-m1b.log`: 2 passed). So the fix pass 13 proposes does not have to break either test. What is true is narrower: the two tests' names, and the twin's docstring ("there is no use in the command picking a second"), state the shared name as a rule. That is a wording matter and stops no fix.

**M6 (confirmed, raised to Important).** I re-applied the four mutants together in a fresh copy (d22). The whole suite, `test_cmake` and `test_transcripts` included, ends with the baseline's three environmental failures. Each effect reproduced, every command in a process of its own (`eff/cli-effects.txt`). `ddd id a.ddd.json` without `--assign` exits 0 and writes an id, where the tree exits 2 and leaves the file untouched. `check --format xml` exits 1 with the text report, where the tree exits 2. `generate a2l` of the demo, with neither `--byte-order` nor `--image`, writes `BYTE_ORDER MSB_FIRST`, where the tree writes `MSB_LAST`. And `_port('65535')` is refused. I raise the grade for the byte order. That default is what every CMake build reaches when it states no `BYTE_ORDER` and takes no addresses from the image, because `cmake/Ddd.cmake:578-579` passes `--byte-order` only when one is given. `tests/test_cli.py:3772-3773` pins the constant the help names, not the default the generate path applies. So a one-token regression would give every such project an a2l with the wrong byte order, and the whole suite would stay green. That is a gap in front of wrong output an integrator would ship, which is Important.

**I1 (confirmed, with corrections).** I copied pass 22's probe file unchanged into my pristine copy and ran it there (`logs/p22-probes.log`, `ddd.__file__` that copy). All ten probes fail, each for the reason the pass gives. The run's two passing tests are `TestAClosedPipe`'s own, which pytest collects through the probe file's import. I then put pass 22's crude fixes into a fresh copy (`fx22`, the two patches in `logs/`): a stage name per write with the bytes compared again before the rename, and withdrawal limited to the files the run reported on. Three probes then pass (pass 13 I1, pass 13 C2, pass 10 I1), as the pass says. My whole-suite run of the same tree is green except for the three environmental failures and one rename race of pass 19 M1, so no test in the suite fails on any of these defects. There are three corrections. First, the ten probes cover eight defects: pass 13 C1 has two probes, and pass 19 I3 is probed with and without `--format json`. Passes 10, 13 and 19 found more than that by hand (pass 10 I5 to I13, pass 13 I2 to I6, pass 19 I1 and I2 have no probe), so "every failure" is too wide. Second, the probe of pass 19 I3 without `--format json` sees an in-process exit 0. Verify-19 showed that this 0 does not survive a real process, which exits 120 there. Only the json case probes the defect a user meets. Third, the suite does build the second actor in other tests: `saving_while_analysing` saves inside the analysis window in four tests, `tests/test_lsp.py:637` and `:5074` serve one component in two images, and several tests open a buffer unlike the disk. It just asks them something else, as the pass's own table shows. Important stands, because three of the eight defects are Critical after verification (pass 13 C1, C2, and I1 as raised).

**M4 (confirmed for two of three, corrected).** PG48, the 503's drain deleted, survives the whole suite in my copy a22. PL06, the `_forget()` after a rename deleted, survives it in b22b. PQ09 does not survive. With `_CASELESS = False`, the run b22 failed `tests/test_gui_queries.py::test_case_is_folded_on_windows_alone`, and so did a run of PQ09 alone (`logs/s-PQ09.log`: 1 failed, 430 passed). That test, at `:237-238`, asserts `queries_module._CASELESS is (sys.platform == "win32")`. Pass 22's line map could not select it, because it reads the constant and runs no line of the module. So the case folding is pinned on Windows, which is where it matters; on Linux the mutant changes nothing. It is still true that no test spells a served directory in another case. That gap is about behaviour, though, and the guard M4 lists as a survivor is killed.

**M5 (confirmed, one of twelve corrected).** I re-applied twelve of M5's survivors in fresh copies (a22, b22b, c22b). Eleven survive the whole suite: `header` and the struct dropped from `SETTABLE`, `y_axis`, `bits`, `entry["from"]` misspelt, `.css` served as `text/html`, `file-kind`, the input role words, `all` read as `any`, `startswith` as `endswith`, and `errors="replace"` dropped. The twelfth is the big-endian DWARF-2 bitfield, `elf.py:787` with `*` read as `//`. It is killed: four tests of `tests/test_elf.py::TestTheMatrix` fail on it, for the `[armeb]` and `[powerpc]` images ('b' found at bit 0 for 8, 'trim' at 2 for 144). They fail in the whole-suite run c22 and again with the mutant alone (`logs/s-787.log`). Those tests read committed images through a fixture, which is probably why pass 22's line map did not select them. The external kind dropped whole was not re-run.

**M9 (confirmed, numbers corrected).** I ran the whole suite on my pristine copy twice, alone. With the default options, coverage and its gate included, it took 643 s and reached 100 % (pass 22: 674 s). With `--no-cov` it took 480 s for 7,042 tests (pass 22: 562 s, with two mutation workers beside it). `test_cmake` took 162 s (34.9 %) and `test_gui_server` 124 s (26.6 %), 61.5 % together, and the other tests 179 s. As the pass says, the server file's cost is spread: 13 tests take over a second, 14.3 s together, and the median is 0.52 s. There is no marker, `requirements-dev.txt` has no `pytest-xdist`, and the gate is in `addopts`. Two corrections. With `--no-cov` it is eight minutes here, not nine. And "nothing smaller than a file can be asked for" is too strong, since the developer page itself recommends `-k` (`docs/developer_documentation.rst:406-407`). "A couple of minutes" is wrong either way; pass 20 M11 found that sentence first.

## Pass 23: the test suite of the page

> **Read this first.** The page has two suites that differ in kind. Vitest holds `api`, `lib` and
> `state` to 100 % coverage with tests that read like specifications, and it earns the gate: with its
> hangs it kills 88 % of the mutants there that compile, in five seconds. The 294 journeys are the
> only test of the other 64 % of the page's code, by the design's own account; they are careful,
> isolated, retry-free, drive the real `ddd gui`, pin behaviour and not pixels, and execute 97.5 to
> 100 % of the screens' lines - yet they kill only 52 % of the `.tsx` folders' compiled mutants, and on
> `lib` code they catch half of what Vitest catches (I2). None of the page defects passes 15 and 16
> found by hand fails any test; each fails a journey of 5 to 18 lines (I1). Everything cited lives
> in `SCRATCH/pass-23/` (`notes.md` is the working log, including four harness defects of mine and
> their repair; `evidence/` holds what outlives the copies).

**Harness defects of mine, repaired** (`notes.md`): (1) the first line map kept one coverage entry
per journey, and 27 journeys load the page twice, so code reached only after a `goto` or a reload
read as unreached: found by a direct mutant (`ValuesPage.tsx:283`), fixed, and the 19 survivors whose
selection grew asked again; (2) Python's text mode wrote CRLF on the first restore, caught by the
restore check before any outcome was recorded; (3) ties in the journey order were first broken by
duration, which put the long, specialised journeys past the cap (`UpdatingNote.tsx:26`'s killer
ranked 148 of 278): since then a hash, and the earlier survivors were asked again; (4) a Vitest run
that hung (300 s) was recorded as no kill: counted as hung, as pass 22 counts it (2 mutants).

### Strengths

- **The journeys pin behaviour, and pin it hard.** 1,591 `getByRole`, 203 reads of what was written
  back to disk, 201 `toHaveText` and many exact sentences; not one screenshot. Nearly every Apply in
  `keys.spec.ts`, `values.spec.ts`, `skeleton.spec.ts` is followed by the file read back. The twenty
  CSS and geometry checks are deliberate (a module dimmed, a dashed border for a file that did not
  load, a focus outline, an alert above the canvas).
- **They reach almost everything, by design.** Each tab's states (reading, failing, kept, stale,
  refused, failed by the server) are rows of part 19b's and 19c's plans with a journey each, and the
  line map agrees: journeys execute 99.7 % of `app`'s mapped lines, 98.7 % of `components`', 97.5 % of
  `screens'`, all of `ui`'s, 96.9 % of `lib`'s.
- **The unit tests are good tests.** Exact expected values, parametrised refusals, domain names
  (`refusals.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`); Vitest, with its two hangs, kills 94 of the 107 compiled mutants of `api`,
  `lib`, `state` (88 %); of the twelve that live, nine are equivalent (a leaked listener, a key's
  order, a timing default) and three are real gaps (Test gaps). It cannot reach a `.tsx` at all: 16 of 16 such mutants
  asked of it lived, as its module graph says they must.
- **No retries anywhere** (`playwright.config.ts` sets none; no `test.retry`, `skip`, `fixme` or
  `slow`), one `waitForTimeout` (16 ms in a bounded settle, `demo.ts:166`): a flaky journey goes red.
  Part 19c's hunts ran every journey five times on three legs and worked their two failures to a
  cause rather than retrying them (plan, 1913-1925, 2083-2084).
- **Isolation holds, and so does the suite under load.** Each journey serves its own copy on port 0
  in a fresh context; ten null mutants ran ten different subsets of 5 to 60 journeys under six to
  eight parallel runners at 90-99 % CPU and all lived. Of 779 journey runs with no mutant (coverage,
  nulls, the loaded flake sample) 775 passed, the 4 failures all one fixture bound (M2); on a quiet
  machine 229 of 229 passed (21 timing-sensitive journeys ten times each, the chain journey ten
  times, the three large ones three times), which agrees with part 19c's hunts.
- **The fixtures fail with a reason, and the journeys fail when their fixture does not do its job.**
  `fixtures.ts:209-216`, `303-387` bound and name their waits; the helpers have journeys of their own
  (`helpers.spec.ts`, 11); with every drift helper a no-op, all 49 journeys that call one fail, none
  vacuously (M5 is about what they say).
- **The story screenshots add something real for components.** Of six mutants the journeys let
  through in `components` and `ui`, the stories catch four (`UpdatingNote` inverted, 16 pictures;
  a class in `UnitPanelView`, 2; the unused count of `UnitsTableView`, 4; the "Type" column header,
  4).
- **The quick loop is quick where the gate is**: `tsc` 0.6 s (TypeScript 7's native compiler),
  Vitest 4.5 s with coverage for 959 tests, Biome under a second, a build 2.2 s. One spec file runs
  in 1.5 to 92 s (median journey 2.5 s), `npx playwright test e2e/<file>.spec.ts:<line>` runs one
  journey. The whole suite: 13.0 min serial on this machine (the coordinator's baseline), 6.1 min on
  the Linux PC (plan, 1931) and 6.8 to 9.9 min a CI leg in its last runs (plan, 1891-1910).

### Issues

#### Critical

None. No survivor is a present defect: each is a wrong program the suite would let through. The
present defects are passes 15 and 16's, and none has a test (I1).

#### Important

- **I1. No test fails on any of the page defects passes 15 and 16 found by hand; each fails a
  journey of 5 to 18 lines built from the suite's own fixtures and helpers.**
  `SCRATCH/pass-23/evidence/p23-probes.spec.ts`, run against the tree's own build
  (`evidence/probes-on-tree.txt`, `evidence/probe-p16C1-on-tree.txt`): 10 failed, the control
  passed, each for the reason its pass gave:

  | pass 15 I1 | an enabled `Apply to 2 files` while the field reads `km/h`; pressed, `rpm` is written | 15, 9 |

  Two pass once their defect is crudely fixed in a copy (`evidence/crude-fixes.patch`:

  Others of the two passes are as cheap: pass 15 I3 (a second page opening another project, about
  20 lines), pass 16 I1 and I3 (a long value's `scrollWidth`, two cells typed; under 10 each), the

  *Why it is structural*: the journeys walk every state a plan row names, through `.fill()` (151
  times; never `pressSequentially` or `keyboard.type`), one key, one document, one revision at a
  time; each hand-found defect needs the second thing - the key the panel moves to next, text left in

  shape as pass 22 I1 on the Python side. *Change* (S, an hour or so each): land each fix with its
  probe; make driving a field with key handling (grid cells, choosers) by `pressSequentially` a rule
  of the journeys (open question 2).

- **I2. The journeys alone guard 64 % of the page's code, and they execute far more of it than they
  check: they kill 52 % of its compiled mutants where Vitest kills 88 % of the logic folders'.**
  `components`, `screens`, `ui`, `app` (10,581 of the page's 16,570 runtime lines) are outside Vitest

### Status of the 2026-09-15 findings in this area

None: the 2026-09-15 review predates the page (its milestone 1 is dated 2026-09-17) and has no
finding on the page's tests.

### Open questions

1. **What guards the decisions in the `.tsx` files: the journeys, a unit gate, or moving them out?**
   Part 19b's spec makes the journeys "the screens' only test" and grew them to 294; I2 shows that
   executing a line is not checking it. (a) The journeys stay the guard, and each new decision lands
   with a journey shown to fail on more than the one change its row names; (b) a DOM environment for
   Vitest (happy-dom, jsdom or Vitest's browser mode; none is a dependency today) and the 100 % gate
   widened to `components`, `ui`, `screens`, `app`; (c) pass 3 I7's direction, the decisions moved
   into `lib/` where the gate already holds them. (c) is cheapest per decision and keeps one gate;
   (b) catches most for the least restructuring.
2. **Is typing key by key, rather than `.fill()`, a rule for the journeys?** Yes makes pass 16 C1's
   class of defect a gate at a cost of seconds per journey; no means every key handler (grid cells,
   choosers, type-to-find) is tested by nothing.
3. **Is a stock Windows machine, with Defender scanning, a supported place to run the journeys?** Yes
   means room in the fixtures' 20 s and 30 s bounds and a smaller chain fixture (M2); no means the
   developer page says the journeys are for CI and Linux, and how long they take there.

### Test gaps

Beyond those passes 3, 15 and 16 listed (not repeated here):
- the ten probes of I1, each a ready journey (`evidence/p23-probes.spec.ts`);
- the behaviours of I2 no journey checks, and three in `lib` and `state` no test pins: `"types"` dropped
  from `SHOWN` (`findings.ts:324`: a routeless finding in a types file would read "has no page yet";
  `findings.test.ts:537-558` covers `project` only), a first poll that fails stopping the follow
  with no retry (`revisions.ts:36`: the retry is tested only after a success), and a path whose
  second part is empty after a non-empty first (`C://x`) read as a network root (`paths.ts:38`);
- states no journey draws (`evidence/unreached.txt`, 102 mapped lines in 18 files): the findings list
  inside a constant's, a raster's and a section's panel (`ConstantPanelView.tsx:165-172`,
  `RasterPanelView.tsx:223-230`, `SectionPanelView.tsx:193-200`); the section's and raster's stale
  refusal (M4); the "Updating the findings…" placeholder of a unit's, a section's and a raster's
  panel (`UnitPanel.tsx:223-225`, `SectionPanel.tsx:241-243`, `RasterPanel.tsx:236-238`); the
  component page's "is no longer declared in the open project" (`ComponentPage.tsx:234-236`); a
  type's "Nothing in the project uses" (`TypePanelView.tsx:180`); typing a section's access
  (`SectionPanel.tsx:259-262`);
- what the CI job lets through, read off the campaign: half of the compiled behaviour changes in the
  screens; any change of a screen's look (no screen has a story); anything only a key, a modified
  click or a second document shows; accessibility (no check, `axe-core` unused); Firefox, Safari and
  macOS (KNOWN, plan 1962); the server half of a journey on Python 3.13 and 3.14 (the job runs 3.12,
  `ci.yml:195`; pytest covers the server there);
- no journey runs with an `actionTimeout`, so none can say which control was missing (M3); nothing
  checks that the pages served are the ones just built (M1).

### Assessment

The page's suite is two suites of different worth. Vitest is the strong one: specification-like
tests over `api`, `lib` and `state`, a 100 % gate that means something, nine in ten compiled mutants
killed in five seconds, three small gaps found. The journeys are the honest, careful and expensive one -
294 of them, isolated, retry-free, worked to the cause when they failed, pinning sentences and the
bytes on disk rather than pixels - and they are, by the design's own words, the only test of the
two thirds of the page that lives in `.tsx` files. There the numbers turn: they execute almost
every line and check about half of what changes on it, and on `lib` code, where both run, they catch
half of what Vitest catches. Every defect passes 15 and 16 found by hand goes through all 294,
because none types key by key, presses Apply with text still in a field, or builds a second key,
document or event, and a journey of 5 to 18 lines would have caught each one. Around that sit the
costs of a large browser suite: 13 minutes here, a fixture bound that a loaded Windows machine
misses, 60 s lost per missing control, a pair of helper files that took 53 commits in seven weeks,
and journeys tied to the demo's layout and geometry. The CI job runs them well; what it lets
through is exactly what they do not look at.

`SCRATCH/pass-24/` (every path below is relative to it). Everything ran in copies made fresh from the tree with

### Strengths

- **The dictionary has one writer.** `ddd dump -o` and `generate all --dictionary` write byte-identical files for the
  demo, and so does `generate --address-map ... --dictionary` (addresses never enter the dictionary); `compare` reads
  the one as a replacement for the other (`seam-dict/`).
- **Name grammars live once.** `C_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN`, `IDENTIFIER_MAX_LENGTH`, the section, raster and type patterns
  are defined in `models/common.py:57-155` and imported by the language server's rename (`lsp/navigation.py:780`); the
  page holds no copy and leaves the refusal to the server's plan.
- **Positions are counted as the protocol counts them, both ways**: outgoing in UTF-16 code units
  (`lsp/ranges.py:232-245`), incoming the same (`:163-171`, a non-BMP character counted two).
- **The page never builds what it writes.** `POST /api/edit` carries the operations of the server's own plan back
  (`contract.py:1618-1666`, `lib/units.ts:208-216`), the page adding only the label; query types are generated from
  the server's models, and `encodeURIComponent` on the page agrees with `parse_qs` on the server (`server.py:697`).
- **Shared copies where the code shares**: build records are found by one function for the editor and the GUI
  (`gui/session.py:54, 248, 569` call `lsp.discovery.discover`); the checks a lone file holds back are derived once
  from the registry (`diagnostics.py:270-273`) for the command line and the language server.
- **The layer table holds for the modules it names**, measured: no import cycle among top-level imports; `elf.py`
  imports nothing of `ddd`; each backend imports only `backends.base`, `ir` and `models`; `lsp` imports no backend; the
  toolbox only `analysis`, `diagnostics`, `elf`, `loading`; `plugins` reaches a backend for typing alone
  (`split/graph.txt`).
- **Bitfield members are kept out of the A2L** rather than given a guessed mask (`backends/a2l/model.py:355-370`), so
  no record can contradict the C compiler's bit allocation, big-endian included.

### Issues

#### Critical

None.

#### Important

- **I1. `<target>.ddd`, the module's own component check, ignores the image's `STRICT` and `SEVERITY`: green where the
  build is red, red where it is green.**
  Location: `cmake/Ddd.cmake:322-324` (`check "${description}" --standalone`, no `-W`, no `--strict`), against
  `docs/build_integration.rst:301-305` ("A tool that ignores it reports a different set of findings than the build
  does ... the same working tree would be clean in one place and failing in the other ... the three cannot drift
  apart") and the comment at `cmake/Ddd.cmake:180-181`.
  Trigger: components `sensor` (outputs `Speed` and `SPEED`) and `reader`; `ddd_generate(fw ... STRICT)`: `ninja`
  exit 1, `error[name-similar]`; `ninja sensor.ddd` exit 0, the same finding as a warning. With `_Speed` for `SPEED`
  and `SEVERITY reserved-identifier=warning` instead: `ninja` exit 0 and `fw.exe` runs; `ninja sensor.ddd` exit 1,
  `error[reserved-identifier]`. The build record beside the build says `"strict": true` and
  `"severity": ["reserved-identifier=warning"]` respectively, and the language server and the GUI apply it, so the
  module's own target is the one surface that disagrees with the build (`build.ninja:113` shows its command).
  Evidence: reproduced, `seam-cmake/transcript.txt`, `seam-cmake/b-strict.*.log`, `b-relax.*.log`.
  Consequence: the supplier check the page offers (`build_integration.rst:77-79`) passes a component the
  integrator's ci then rejects, and a project that must relax a check project-wide (pass 6 M11: an external type
  named `size_t`) gets a `<target>.ddd` that can never pass. Fix: `ddd_add_component` takes no `STRICT` or
  `SEVERITY`, and a component can be linked into several images; either give it the keywords, or have the target
  take the policy of a named image's record, or say on the page that it checks under the default policy and drop
  "cannot drift" (S).

#### Minor

- **M1. A run refuses its own files as "outside the output directory" when another process creates that directory
  meanwhile (lead V9 settled).**
  Location: `src/ddd/backends/base.py:228` and `:233-234`; the same resolve-and-compare in `Manifest` at `:148`,
  `:181-184` and `:199-200`.
  Cause: `render` resolves the output directory once and each file again, then compares with `is_relative_to`. On
  Windows CPython's `ntpath.realpath` strips the `\\?\` prefix only if its second `_getfinalpathname` fails with the
  same error as the first (`ntpath.py:745-749`); a directory created between the two calls turns
  `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` (3) into `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (2), the prefix stays, and a `\\?\` path is compared with a
  plain one.
  Trigger: `ddd generate c demo.ddd.json -o out` into a fresh `out` while anything else creates `out`: a second
  `ddd` run (verify-19 M11's 9 of 12 failures), or a parallel build's `mkdir -p`. Exit 2, `ddd: backend 'c' writes
  outside the output directory: //?/<work>/o302/SensorHub.h`, nothing written.
  Evidence: reproduced deterministically, `lead2/det.txt` (winerror 3 then 2 on `out_race/ddd_globals.c`, exit 2;
  the control writes all seven files), and with real processes, `lead2/race_mkdir.txt` (2 of 400 runs refused when my
  `os.mkdir` landed in the window, delays 0.506 and 0.521 s of a 0.61 s run). The `Manifest` copies read off: the same
  race there leaves a written file out of the record, or a stale one in place, in silence. Fix: create the directory
  before resolving it, and compare paths resolved alike (S). Minor: it needs a concurrent creation and fails loud.

- **M2. A scroll while a chooser's list is open throws away what was typed, and the next keys append to the old
  spelling: "km", one wheel notch, "/h" plans `rpm` to `rpm/h` across 67 files (lead V8 settled).**
  Location: `gui/src/ui/ComboBox.tsx:108-112` (`onOpenChange(false)` calls `onClose`), `screens/UnitPanel.tsx:246`
  and `:256` (the field reads `typed ?? to ?? name`; closing drops `typed`); React Aria closes the popover on any
  scroll of an ancestor of the field (`react-aria/dist/private/overlays/useCloseOnScroll.mjs`). Against
  `ComboBox.tsx:45-49`, which lists the list closing "by Enter, Escape, Tab, ▾ or the focus leaving the field" only.
  Trigger: a generated "many" project of 2,000 declarations, Units tab, `rpm`, the `Rename rpm to` field (at y 908 in a
  1280x800 window, below the fold): select all, type `km`, turn the wheel one notch up: the list closes and the field
  reads `rpm`; type `/h`: `rpm/h`; Enter: "Apply to 67 files", whose sentence names the files and not the new
  spelling. V8's `rpmpm2` is the same mechanism: the driver's scroll into view fires about 20 ms after the field
  takes the focus, and a key typed in that window is dropped (`trace_key4.txt`: `rpmr`, list open at 298 ms, scroll
  at 299 ms, list closed and `rpm` back at 322 ms; with a one-second pause the key is kept; nothing is lost when the
  field is already in view, `human.txt`). The typed text equal to the unit's own spelling closes the list too
  (`lib/projectUnits.ts:136` adds no "As typed" entry), harmlessly.
  Evidence: reproduced in Edge, `lead1/human.txt`, `rename_keys2.txt`, `trace_key2.txt` to `trace_key4.txt`. Same root
  as pass 15 I1 (text typed and left is dropped), a trigger it does not have: the reader never left the field. Minor:
  the field shows the composed spelling before Enter, and Undo takes it back. Fix: drop what was typed only on Escape
  or on leaving the field, not on every close React Aria makes (S).

### Status of the 2026-09-15 findings in this area

None in this area: the sweep's seams fall in the areas whose passes (9, 10, 13, 14, 19) already tabulated the
2026-09-15 findings.

### Open questions

- **Which policy should `<target>.ddd` apply (I1)?** A component can sit in several images with different `STRICT` and
  `SEVERITY`. "The image's" means a keyword or a record to name the image; "the default" means the page's
  "cannot drift" sentence goes and suppliers are told their check is not the build's; "its own" means
  `ddd_add_component` grows `STRICT` and `SEVERITY`, a second place to keep them in step.
- **May React Aria close a chooser's list behind the reader's back (M2)?** Keeping its close-on-scroll means the page
  must keep the typed text across such closes; turning it off means a list that stays put while the page scrolls under
  it.

### Test gaps

- No test runs `<target>.ddd` under a project with `STRICT` or `SEVERITY` (`tests/test_cmake.py:1642-1725` checks
  components wrong by default only).
- No journey types into a chooser key by key: every one uses `fill()` (`gui/e2e/units.spec.ts:287`,
  `project-units.spec.ts:84, 237, 371`, `shared.spec.ts:158, 177`; no `pressSequentially` or `keyboard.type` in
  `gui/e2e`), and none scrolls while a list is open.
- The confinement of `render` is tested only against real escapes (`tests/test_backends.py:378`,
  `tests/test_plugins.py:2005-2071`), never against an output directory that appears while a run resolves it.

### Assessment

The code that fell between the passes is small: every source file of the scope was claimed read in full by some pass,
and the stories and generated types are the only parts nobody read. So the sweep's weight is in the seams and the
leads, and there the picture is better than the area reports suggest: where two sides share a definition they agree
(one dictionary writer, one name grammar, one record discovery, one held-back set, UTF-16 positions both ways, the
page echoing the server's plans), and the disagreements come where a rule was written twice. Measured, the rules held
twice are: the severity policy (command line, build record, CMake's build-info/check/generate, and the module's own
`<target>.ddd`, the only one that ignores it: I1); the raster rename (the GUI's copy escapes `a"b`, `rules/raster_rename.txt`,
the language server's writes it raw: pass 10 I9); the constant rename (both copies leave a `condition` spelling the old
name); the `*.ddd.json` case rule (pass 5 M14); the kind of a file (pass 2 M4; CMake 4.3 agrees with the loader on a
byte order mark, `seam-bom/`); the unit spelling (pass 15 M10); the number grammar (15 M13); the 4,300-digit guard
(17 M2); the retry on replace (19 M1); the request size (3 I8, 15 I4); and the line break, where `lsp/ranges.py:79`
splits at `\n` alone while the protocol also breaks at a bare `\r` (read off, not run; unnumbered Minor). The import graph
confirms passes 2's account: 87 modules, 363 edges, no cycle among top-level imports, the cycles it names among deferred
ones, and table rows true of the modules they list. Both leads were real and are settled with their causes (M1, M2).
Lines on earlier candidates: **10 I10 is wider**: the GUI's constant rename (`GET /api/constant-plan`, then
`POST /api/edit`) also leaves `"condition": "CELLS > 2"` beside `Big[SLOTS]`, check clean, `#if CELLS > 2` in the C
(`rules/const_rename.txt`), so the rule is wrong in both of its copies. **2 I5 is slightly wider**: `compare.py`, which
the page calls "the second consumer of the contract", is also imported by the analysis at top level
(`analysis.py:18-24`, its field comparison), so the front end depends on it. **19 M11 stands**, its third failure mode
being M1 here.
